answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a umber as the anchor of the cost.
